participants.note: Concept ACK; raised concern about global callback leaking state between unit tests
suggested dropping local user_data for a simple function pointer
objected to prematurely limiting logging/tracing API in a way difficult to reverse

claims.harm: Prematurely restricts the kernel logging API in a way difficult to reverse without notable simplification
claims.quote: I think it would be a mistake to limit functionality of the logging/debuging/tracing API prematurely, in a way that seems difficult to reverse and does not seem to provide a noticeable simplification
claims.settled_by_quote: It's a +76/-72 diff, I don't think this will be particularly hard to reverse? If you're talking about breaking the interface: it is unversioned and we're quite explicit about breaking it when we want to

claims.harm: Global logging callback leaks state across unit tests if not reset
claims.quote: Even though this function is scoped to this test, it now enables logging for all the the other unit tests too. Maybe add another call to set the callback to null at the end of the test?
claims.settled_by_quote: Yeah, this seems like the most elegant approach to me. In fact, I think it makes sense to not expose the free logging functions at all in the wrapper. The `Logger` class should offer all required functionality

claims.harm: Tests installing global callback leak state unless explicitly cleared
claims.quote: any test that installs the global logging callback now needs to clear it before returning to prevent state leakage into later tests.
claims.settled_by_quote: The `Logger` class should offer all required functionality, in a way that is much harder to abuse. Thank you both for your ideas and suggestions. I've updated the PR with this approach.

support.reason: Not having separate connections seems simpler, clients can multiplex themselves, and it is pragmatic

result.notes: Initial assessment of discussion. ryanofsky raised an approach concern about prematurely limiting logging API, which author countered with rationale on unversioned C API and small diff, with no further pushback. Test leakage concerns by sedited and w0xlt were resolved with an RAII Logger class in the C++ wrapper.
